_comment: Shared golden-master fixture for calculateNextReminder (src/utils.js and web/src/lib/medication-utils.ts) — and eventually its Kotlin port. Every 'expectedUtc' was computed independently via moment-timezone (not by calling calculateNextReminder itself) and cross-checked against both JS implementations before being committed here. 'now' overrides the function's 4th parameter; every real production caller omits it. A vector with expectThrow=true must throw, not return a value — that is the deliberate contract for an empty/invalid reminder_times array (src/utils.js's own comment explains why: callers must pre-filter, same as src/scheduler.js's DATA PROBLEM guard). See db/migrations/migration_dose_days_2026_08_10.sql for dose_days semantics (0=Sun..6=Sat, null=daily). Android M0: port this exact set of cases before writing any Kotlin scheduling code (see CLAUDE.md Android section).

vectors.name: rolls to tomorrow when today's time has passed, IST
multi-time day picks the earliest time still ahead
once-weekly, due today and time not yet passed (offset 0)
once-weekly, due today but time already passed — rolls a full 7 days, not a fortnight (offset 7)
once-weekly evening dose, different weekday/time from the other offset-7 case — rolls a full 7 days
vectors.notes: 2026-08-12 and 2026-08-19 are both Wednesdays. Same offset-7 mechanic as the vector above, deliberately at a different weekday + time so the fixture isn't only ever exercising Monday-morning doses.

vectors.name: doseDays [0,1,2,3,6] — real-data pattern, skips excluded Thu/Fri to the next included Saturday
vectors.notes: 2026-08-13/14 (Thu/Fri) are excluded; 2026-08-15 is the next included day (Saturday).

vectors.name: Asia/Calcutta (legacy IANA alias) resolves identically to Asia/Kolkata — real-data finding, live medications hold both spellings
vectors.notes: Asia/Calcutta is the tzdata 'backward' link Asia/Kolkata was renamed from in 2018; both names carry byte-identical DST/offset rules. Verified independently on the JDK (java.time.ZoneId.of("Asia/Calcutta").getRules().equals(ZoneId.of("Asia/Kolkata").getRules()) -> true) as well as via moment-timezone here — expectedUtc is deliberately identical to the very first vector in this file, computed with 'Asia/Kolkata', to prove the alias produces the exact same instant, not just a close one.

vectors.name: DST spring-forward, America/New_York — after the transition day uses the post-transition (EDT, UTC-4) offset
vectors.notes: US DST 2026 starts 2026-03-08 02:00 EST -> 03:00 EDT. 09:00 on the transition day is already EDT.

vectors.name: DST spring-forward, America/New_York — day before the transition still uses EST (UTC-5), for offset comparison against the previous vector
DST fall-back, Europe/London — after the transition day uses the post-transition (GMT, UTC+0) offset
vectors.notes: UK DST 2026 ends 2026-10-25 02:00 BST -> 01:00 GMT. 09:00 on the transition day is already GMT.

vectors.name: DST fall-back, Europe/London — day before the transition still uses BST (UTC+1), for offset comparison against the previous vector
midnight edge — just before local midnight, rolls to the upcoming midnight less than an hour away
midnight edge — now exactly equals a candidate instant; isAfter is strict, so it rolls to the NEXT day, not the same instant
garbage dose_days (matches no real weekday) falls back to tomorrow at the first sorted time rather than never firing
vectors.notes: The DB CHECK constraint makes this unreachable in practice; the DB write path can never produce it. Exists to lock in the fail-safe behavior if it ever were.

vectors.name: empty reminder_times array — must throw, never silently substitute a value
vectors.notes: This is the drift that was fixed 2026-08-10: web/src/lib/medication-utils.ts used to silently return `new Date()` here while src/utils.js threw. Every caller of calculateNextReminder must pre-filter an empty/null reminder_times array before calling (see the DATA PROBLEM guards in src/scheduler.js, web/src/app/api/cron/tick/route.ts, and the medications/new and medications/[id] forms) — the throw is a deliberately unreachable backstop, not the primary safety mechanism.
